\chapter{Project Management and Development Evidence}
\section{Work Completed}\label{ch9:sec:done}
Eleven of Iteration 1's fourteen work packages are merged (Table~\ref{ch6:tab:wps}). One command, \texttt{py -m runner diagnose}, takes a failing test through ordered re-execution, polluter search, minimisation, bytecode evidence and the outcome decision to a schema-validated report, and has done so for all seven fixture cases (\path{eval/reports/}). Nine of the ten proposal actions are complete (Section~\ref{ch3:sec:register}).

\section{Work Remaining}\label{ch9:sec:remaining}
Before the Mid evaluation: this report and the evidence worksheet, the tag \texttt{mid-eval-v1}, and a rehearsed demonstration (W11--W13). After it, Iteration 2's commitments (Section~\ref{ch3:sec:it2}) and the deviations still open in Table~\ref{ch3:tab:deviations}: the container, the test--resource graph, the threat model and a first real project end to end.

\section{Repository and Version Control Evidence}\label{ch9:sec:repo}
All code, tests, documents and this report are in one GitHub repository:
\begin{center}\url{https://github.com/zoyaahmad428/FlakeTrace}\end{center}
The working rules are in \path{CONTRIBUTING.md}:
\begin{itemize}
  \item \textbf{Branches} are named after their owner and topic (\texttt{m2/order-runner}, \texttt{docs/report-m2}); since the restructure into one repository (\pr{1}), nothing is committed to \texttt{main} directly.
  \item \textbf{Pull requests} need passing CI and an approval from another member; every pull request was reviewed by a member who did not write it (as stated by the team; Appendix~\ref{app:repository}). A pull-request template asks for the member and area, how the change was verified, its effect on the contracts, and the evidence and GenAI logs.
  \item \textbf{Commits} are made by the member after reading the change, with a title \texttt{[M<N>] <area>: <what changed>} and a \texttt{Verified:} line giving the real command and result.
  \item \textbf{CI} (\path{.github/workflows/ci.yml}) runs four jobs on every pull request on Linux with JDK 8: evaluation tests and the yield report, the fixture's premises, the runner tests and the evidence tests. A second workflow (\path{report.yml}) builds this report's PDF.
\end{itemize}

Reviews found real problems, and the code records them. Two examples from Member 2's reviews of Member 3's report assembly: a merge order in which the command would have crashed with a stack trace instead of exiting with code 3, and report text that said ``given order'' when no order had been given (both noted ``flagged by Member 2'' in \path{eval/report.py}).

Table~\ref{ch9:tab:git} counts the history on \texttt{main} at commit \texttt{4bc3fde} (13 October 2026), before this table was updated (\texttt{git shortlog} and the merge commits). Member 2's commits include three made on 9 October under a second e-mail address. A pull request is credited to the member who wrote most of its commits.

\section{Tools and Tool-Assisted Development}\label{ch9:sec:genai}
All three members used generative AI, and this section discloses it per artefact, as the FYP GenAI guide requires. Every materially assisted code, test or design change is recorded in \path{docs/08-MidEval/genai-register.md} (date, member, tool, level, what was used, what the member changed, how it was verified, what was rejected), with session-level detail in \path{docs/genai-log-m1.md}, \path{-m2.md} and \path{-m3.md}. The levels are those of the guide:
\begin{itemize}
  \item \textbf{L1 supportive:} grammar, formatting, brainstorming, small debugging hints;
  \item \textbf{L2 assisted:} significant code, tests, diagrams or text generated, then reviewed, changed, tested and fully explainable by the member;
  \item \textbf{L3 core-assist:} the AI produced a major module or core feature; the member states what the AI produced, what they added, why it works and its limits;
  \item \textbf{L4 substituted:} the member cannot explain or change it. No artefact is at L4.
\end{itemize}

Two rules applied to all assisted work: the member, not the AI, makes every commit after reading the change (\path{CLAUDE.md}, \path{CONTRIBUTING.md}), and no result is written down unless a command was actually run. Table~\ref{ch9:tab:genai} gives the disclosure per artefact; the counts are rows in the register on 11 October 2026.

\section{Security and Privacy Considerations}\label{ch9:sec:security}
FlakeTrace runs other people's tests, so it executes code it did not write. At Iteration 1:
\begin{itemize}
  \item \textbf{No sandbox.} Tests run as ordinary processes with the user's permissions, with a 120\,s timeout and nothing else. The required rootless container with no network, resource limits and verified cleanup (\path{docs/02-Requirements/non-functional.md}) is not built. Until it is, FlakeTrace should only be used on projects the user trusts, which is the risk register's own fallback.
  \item \textbf{Network.} FlakeTrace's own code makes no network calls. Maven may download the analysed project's dependencies, and the project's tests may use the network themselves.
  \item \textbf{The analysed source is not changed.} Every file except \path{target/} and \path{.git/} is hashed before and after a diagnosis, and the record folder may not be inside the project (Section~\ref{ch5:sec:arch}).
  \item \textbf{Data stays local.} Reports and execution records are written to \texttt{flaketrace-\allowbreak records/}, which git ignores. They contain test names, failure messages with numbers and paths masked, the project's absolute path, its git commit and the operating system; nothing is redacted further and nothing is sent anywhere.
  \item \textbf{AI in the product.} None: generative AI was used to develop FlakeTrace (Section~\ref{ch9:sec:genai}), not inside it.
\end{itemize}

\section{Current Limitations}\label{ch9:sec:limitations}
Each module's limitations are in its own section of Chapter~6. Across the system:
\begin{itemize}
  \item evidence is static only, for two resource families (static fields and system properties);
  \item JUnit 3 and 4 only, run through Maven projects;
  \item a report shows one shared resource; with several polluters the others are named in its limitations;
  \item no diagnosis has yet run end to end on a real project;
  \item no sandbox (Section~\ref{ch9:sec:security});
  \item the budget of 31 shuffled orders is taken from a study of Python projects~\cite{gruber2021flaky}.
\end{itemize}
